name: United States
registration_steps: Check your state's registration deadline (varies by state, usually 15-30 days before election)
Register online at vote.gov or your state's election website
You can also register by mail using the National Voter Registration Form
Or register in person at your DMV, public library, or election office
Provide your state driver's license/ID number or last 4 digits of SSN
Some states offer Same-Day Registration at the polls
voting_steps: Find your polling place at vote.gov or your state election website
Check if your state requires a photo ID (laws vary by state)
Know your state's ID requirements before election day
Arrive at your polling location during voting hours (typically 7am - 8pm)
Check in with poll workers and sign the poll book
Receive your ballot (paper ballot or touchscreen depending on county)
Submit your ballot in the scanner or ballot box
You may receive an 'I Voted' sticker
voting_hours: Varies by state (typically 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM local time)
id_notes: ID requirements vary by state. Some states require photo ID, others accept non-photo documents.
notes: Voting laws vary significantly by state. Check your specific state's requirements at vote.gov. U.S. citizens living abroad can vote using UOCAVA.
